question: Can one shared strict action contract reject interface errors without supplying design decisions, and can the actual tokenizer support constrained output?
scope: CPU engineering prerequisite only; no model sampling, scene edits, optimizer updates or learning claims

dependency.install_policy: wheel-only isolated --target; original environments unchanged; resolution report and full installed-file hashes before checks

contract.identifiers: catalog asset IDs and current furniture IDs only; no inferred hard-retention filter
contract.coordinates: unbounded finite numbers; no reference coordinates, geometry optimizer or target-layout filtering
contract.termination: explicit done with unknown/unmet statement, not auto-success
contract.execution: strict JSON plus schema/reference validation before dispatch; any rejection counted; no correction or retry
contract.decoding: shared across future arms; changes output protocol; no strict old-vs-new causal comparison

acceptance: positive/negative fixtures, actual old-output classification, real-tokenizer prefix walk with EOS boundary; failures preserved and no GPU escalation
